issues.reason: "other halogens" is an article-less plural, and an oblique's object NP follows the ordinary NP rules — a bare plural is the generic kind, and "reserve the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object" licenses exactly this constant — while "other" has no licensed carrier, so leaving it out follows the instruction set's own leave-it-out-rather-than-mis-slot policy (the reviewer's second gap).

The objective-genitive rule indeed does not reach a subjective genitive, but that is the coverage gap the reviewer itself files, and the improvisation is licensed elsewhere: the event-noun's witness IS the eventuality (light-verb rule), and a reciprocal "react with" predicate "stays one event with multiple Agent atoms" exactly as "collided with" does — every atom emitted is true of the sentence and well-typed.

The naming rule states a witness is minted `sk_<class>_<n>` and "the symbol is minted from the class" (`sk_person_1`, never `sk_he_1`), so an initialism of the surface phrase, `sk_ds_1`, violates a stated rule.

gaps_confirmed: subjective genitive on a nominalization ("the reaction of caesium", "the arrival of the train") — only the objective genitive is specified
"other" as an anaphoric contrast determiner on a plural has no encoding
new_gaps: an identity copular clause whose predicate nominal is an event-noun with its own arguments ("the synthesis is a reaction of X with Y"): whether the subject witness absorbs the predicate noun's argument structure, and on which symbol those roles hang, is unstated
repair_summary: Renamed the witness `sk_ds_1` to the class-derived `sk_synthesis_1` in all six atoms; nothing else changed (proof names, atom order, roles and TVs kept).
notes: Splitting "direct synthesis" into synthesis + direct rather than fusing the term of art was not raised as an issue and is defensible under the descriptive-vs-term-of-art test, so it was left alone.
